description: Capella pages routinely cite literal 'Couchbase Server X.Y' version strings, or link to server/ paths, despite Capella being a continuously-deployed product with no discrete version numbers. First found in the 100-page stress test (11 relations across 6 pages) - round 5's 115-page sweep of cloud/n1ql/ found it far more densely: 45 of 115 pages (39%), across nearly every statement/function/clause category (DDL, DML, TCL, function reference, hints, statistics). Density this high across a directory this broad reads less like isolated copy-paste and more like a systemic pattern in how this whole reference tree was authored/adapted from server/'s. Examples across both rounds: cloud/n1ql/n1ql-intro/sysinfo.md carries 'Couchbase Server 8.0' badges; cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md cites 'Server 8.0/7.6.0/7.6.8' and links an absolute /server/8.0/ path; cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/monitoring-n1ql-query.md's sample JSON output includes an edition-tagged version string ('7.0.0-4960-enterprise') meaningless on Capella; datefun.md alone cites 'Server 8.0' five separate times; using-ai.md cites version strings 7+ times. Several agents independently concluded this reads as server/ content copied with only the product name substituted, not written for Capella's model. A sibling anomaly - Enterprise/Community edition badges (not version strings) on Capella pages, which likewise have no edition split - was found in round 5 and logged separately as docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-edition-badges.json.
foundDuring: poc-100-page-stress-test; recurred far more densely in round 5 (115-page cloud/n1ql/ sweep)
